title: Competition between on-site and off-site pairing phases and surface spectra in superconducting wallpaper fermion systems
abstract: We theoretically investigate the competition between on-site and off-site pairings in superconducting topological crystalline insulators hosting wallpaper fermions, a class of surface states protected by nonsymmorphic symmetries. In-plane nearest-neighbor pair hopping stabilizes the $\mathrm{A_{1u}}$ phase, while off-site pairing channels yield additional dominant phases with $\mathrm{B_{2u}}$ and $\mathrm{E_u}$ representations. We further show that the $\mathrm{B_{2u}}$ pairing state supports the hybridization between wallpaper-fermion spectra themselves, whereas a representative time-reversal-invariant nematic $\mathrm{E_u}$ state exhibits spectral hybridization between wallpaper fermion and double Majorana Kramers pairs, yielding twisted surface energy spectra. These results demonstrate that the twisted dispersions arising from hybridization phenomena persist in the presence of off-site pairing interactions.
summary: This theoretical work explores how competing on-site and off-site superconducting pairing interactions affect the surface physics of wallpaper fermion systems. By solving the gap equation and analyzing topological invariants, the authors identify that off-site pairing stabilizes specific phases ($B_{2u}, E_u$) that manifest distinct, symmetry-protected 'twisted' surface energy spectra. This highlights the crucial role of pairing symmetry in determining observable surface electronic properties.
main_problem: The study investigates the competition between different superconducting pairing symmetries (on-site vs. off-site) and how this competition dictates the resulting surface electronic spectra in superconducting wallpaper fermion systems.
main_result: The incorporation of off-site pairing interactions stabilizes $B_{2u}$ and $E_u$ phases, which both support characteristic 'twisted surface dispersions' arising from hybridization with either the wallpaper fermions themselves or double Majorana Kramers pairs.
method: The analysis employs a mean-field approach, solving the linearized gap equation derived from the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian, and calculating topological invariants using symmetry analysis along specific high-symmetry lines.
model_or_system: The system is superconducting topological crystalline insulators hosting wallpaper fermions, modeled by a tight-binding Hamiltonian on a tetragonal four-sublattice structure. The superconductivity is introduced via pairing interactions ($H_{int}$) analyzed through its irreducible representations ($D_{4h}$).
key_observables:
Superconducting pairing phases ($A_{1u}, B_{2u}, E_u$), surface energy spectra, and topological invariants ($
u_{\pm}^{DIII[U]}$).
important_parameters: Interaction parameters ($\alpha_{\parallel}, \alpha_{\perp}$), on-site interaction strength ($V_0$), and chemical potential ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mean-field approximation and the use of symmetry-protected topological invariants to classify the superconducting state.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the tetragonal four-sublattice model and the bulk/surface Brillouin zones, while the appendix details the surface spectra along the $ ar{\Gamma}  ar{M}  ar{\Gamma}$ line, showing gap opening and hybridization features.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the model Hamiltonian and the competition between pairing terms. It then uses the gap equation to map the superconducting phase diagram based on symmetry representations. Finally, it analyzes the resulting surface spectra and topological invariants for specific pairing channels.
why_interesting: The detailed symmetry analysis and the focus on hybridization between gapless surface states and superconducting pairing gaps provide a rich theoretical framework relevant to understanding exotic superconducting pairing mechanisms in topological materials.
